title: Animation performance and compositor concepts
learningObjectives: Explain animation performance and compositor concepts and create motion that respects user preferences.

understand.concept: Browser rendering commonly involves style calculation, layout, paint, and compositing. Animating transform and opacity can often be handled efficiently by compositing, while animating layout-affecting properties may trigger more work. Actual performance depends on the browser and page.
understand.whyItMatters: Large or continuous animations can drain battery and cause dropped frames. Measure on representative devices and avoid adding will-change pre-emptively because it can consume resources.
understand.analogy: Some animations move an already painted layer; others require the browser to recalculate and repaint more of the page.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual animation, rendering, and preference handling follow CSS and browser behaviour.

explain.narrative: The example animates transform and opacity. Profile a comparable width animation to understand the difference in rendering work.

examples.explanation: The example animates transform and opacity. Profile a comparable width animation to understand the difference in rendering work.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered example showing the animation or user-preference behaviour.

practise.guidedTask: Compare a transform animation with an animation of width on several cards. Use browser performance tools to measure rather than guessing.
practise.independentTask: Build a small motion-enhanced component. Provide a static or reduced-motion state and test the result with keyboard interaction.
hints: Keep essential content visible without animation.
Test light/dark and forced-colours preferences where relevant.
Measure performance on a representative device.

practice.starterCode: Move me
practice.resetCode: Move me

questions.prompt: Which properties are often efficient candidates for animation?
questions.explanation: These can often be handled by compositing without layout, but performance should still be measured.

questions.prompt: What should happen when a user requests reduced motion?
options: Non-essential movement should be removed or simplified
questions.answer: Non-essential movement should be removed or simplified
questions.explanation: The interface should preserve content and operation while respecting the preference.
